stories.title: Morocco's first female head of government: Symbol or real reform?
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5NfFo Mansouri has been nicknamed the "pasha's daughter" because she comes from a prominent Marrakesh family and her father was formerly a pasha or municipal governor Image: Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP Advertisement After the announcement that Morocco would appoint its first female head of government – Marrakech mayor Fatima Zahra Mansouri – citizens interviewed by local television reporters were mostly enthusiastic. stories.title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'
stories.summary: Image source, Christian Parkinson/ BBC Image caption, Kgomotso Mathekga says a lack of male role models is fuelling violence against women in his neighbourhood By Christian Parkinson Reporting from Johannesburg Published 3 October 2026, 00:56 BST "I witness men hitting women all the time," says Kgomotso Mathekga, 30. "Especially when they are both drunk." "I once had an argument with my girlfriend," he admits, "and I grabbed and slapped her." Mathekga is speaking frankly during a gathering of men aimed at helping reduce the high levels of violence against women in South Africa. The meeting is held in a narrow street in a Johannesburg informal settlement known as Organic Market. It is a maze of corrugated metal shacks and unpaved roads, close to Alexandra township. "Now I feel pain," Mathekga continues. "We broke up and I no longer see my child. I feel like I've contributed to the problems in South Africa, instead of being the gentleman that I know I am." stories.title: Kenya: City Hall Launches Day 2 of 'Operation Okoa Maisha' El Niño Emergency Simulation
stories.summary: Kenya: City Hall Launches Day 2 of 'Operation Okoa Maisha' El Niño Emergency Simulation 2 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Correspondent Nairobi — Nairobi City County has entered the second day of Operation Okoa Maisha, a multi-agency emergency simulation exercise designed to test the city's preparedness and response to the expected El Niño rains. The exercise is being conducted at Central Park, where Nairobi County and its multi-agency partners have established a Command Post to simulate the coordination of emergency operations during a major weather-related incident. The exercise is being undertaken under the "One County, One Plan, One Command" framework, which seeks to strengthen coordination among agencies involved in disaster preparedness, response and recovery. Nairobi County's team, led by Bramwell Simiyu, Chief Officer for Disaster Coordination, together with leaders from participating agencies, is overseeing coordination activities on the second day of the simulation. stories.title: South Africa: Rubber Bullets Fired At Rhodes Graduation Ceremony
stories.summary: South Africa: Rubber Bullets Fired At Rhodes Graduation Ceremony 2 October 2026 GroundUp (Cape Town) By Sindisiwe Tshona and Ndimphiwe Mpongoma Students continued to protest despite a high court interdict A court interdict against protests at Rhodes University did not stop about 100 students from demonstrating outside a graduation ceremony on Friday morning. Police used stun grenades and rubber bullets to disperse the crowd. Students are protesting against the university's new fee payment protocol, which would require many students to pay all their debt before registering for the next year. Police fired stun grenades and rubber bullets to disperse about 100 protesters outside a Rhodes University graduation ceremony for master's and doctoral students in Makhanda on Friday morning. 13 students were arrested. stories.summary: Zambia: African Bishops Express Concern Over the Arrest of Archbishop Banda 2 October 2026 Fides News Agency (Vatican) Lusaka — "On behalf of the Symposium of Episcopal Conferences of Africa and Madagascar (SECAM), we wish to express our fraternal solidarity and prayerful closeness to the Zambia Conference of Catholic Bishops (ZCCB), and in a particular way to His Grace Dr. Alick Banda, Archbishop of Lusaka, at this challenging moment in the life of the Church in Zambia." stories.title: Trump is disappearing refugees into the hands of torturers – and rewarding them handsomely | Tutu Alicante and Uzra Zeya
stories.summary: ‘Adam and everyone held at Hotel Bamy should be released and given the chance to have their asylum claims heard in a country capable of hearing them.’ Photograph: Monika Pronczuk/AP View image in fullscreen ‘Adam and everyone held at Hotel Bamy should be released and given the chance to have their asylum claims heard in a country capable of hearing them.’ Photograph: Monika Pronczuk/AP Trump is disappearing refugees into the hands of torturers – and rewarding them handsomely Tutu Alicante and Uzra Zeya Refugees from third countries are being sent to Equatorial Guinea, where they are often sent back to the very countries they fled F or nearly a year, the Hotel Bamy in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea , has been Adam’s prison. Just days before full-scale fighting resumed, several armed groups which had previously considered each enemies formally announced an alliance with a common goal: To bring down Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's federal government. But this time, the situation looks quite different from the previous conflict: Parties outside the country have been accused of meddling in the situation, with each having their own motives to want to destabilize Abiy's government. This has raised fears about prolonged instability hitting the Horn of Africa. stories.title: Fête nationale en Guinée: une exposition rend hommage aux «compagnons de l'indépendance»
stories.summary: Fête nationale en Guinée: une exposition rend hommage aux «compagnons de l'indépendance» C'est la fête nationale ce vendredi en Guinée, qui a obtenu son indépendance le 2 octobre 1958, quatre jours après le « non » au référendum sur le projet de communauté franco-africaine du général de Gaulle. Pour l'occasion, le gouvernement a consacré une exposition à l'histoire du pays, qui met à l'honneur les « compagnons de l'indépendance », ces leaders politiques qui ont mené la Guinée vers la liberté aux côtés de Sékou Touré. Publié le : 02/10/2026 - 09:50 Modifié le : 02/10/2026 - 15:58 2 min Temps de lecture Ahmed Sékou Touré, premier président de la Guinée (1958-1984), assiste à une réunion, le 11 février 1959. AFP Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite Avec notre correspondant à Conakry , Tangi Bihan Le dramaturge Fodéba Keita, l'homme politique Saïfoulaye Diallo, le syndicaliste Koumandian Keita, la femme politique Loffo Camara… Autant de figures que l'on croise sur les rives du lac Gbassikolo, près du Palais du peuple, au cœur de Conakry. Si le président Sékou Touré (1958-1984) a incarné l'indépendance de la Guinée , il n'a pas mené seul le pays vers la liberté, rappelle Daouda Tamsir Niane, directeur de la Bibliothèque nationale : « Toutes sont des figures qui ont beaucoup agi pour l'indépendance.

stories.title: Première ministre au Maroc, tensions Érythrée-Éthiopie, Embalo attendu en Guinée-Bissau : l’hebdo Afrique
stories.summary: Publicité Première ministre au Maroc, tensions Érythrée-Éthiopie, Embalo attendu en Guinée-Bissau : l’hebdo Afrique Récap Afrique Publié le : 02/10/2026 - 09:25 Modifié le : 02/10/2026 - 16:08 5 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, la nouvelle cheffe du gouvernement marocain, arrive à une réunion à Rabat le 29 septembre 2026. © Abdel Majid Bziouat, AFP • Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri est devenue mardi la première femme cheffe de gouvernement au Maroc . Issue d'une famille de notables de Marrakech, cette femme brune de 50 ans, souvent aperçue derrière ses lunettes à monture foncée, a également été élue députée lors des législatives de mercredi dernier. • L' Éthiopie a accusé jeudi l' Érythrée voisine "d'actes d'hostilité et de belligérance", fermé son ambassade sur place et sommé dix diplomates érythréens de faire leurs valises, Asmara répliquant en rompant ses relations diplomatiques : les tensions sont encore montées en plein conflit dans le nord éthiopien entre armée éthiopienne et groupes antigouvernementaux. • En Guinée-Bissau , dix mois après avoir été renversé par un putsch, l'ex-président en exil, Umaro Sissoco Embalo , a annoncé lundi son retour prochain dans son pays comme "candidat à la présidentielle" du 6 décembre censée rétablir l'ordre constitutionnel. • Plusieurs pays africains se disent prêts à participer à la Force internationale de stabilisation de Gaza , imaginée par Donald Trump , et censée se déployer dans l’enclave palestinienne pour y stabiliser la situation. Le Maroc , l’Ouganda mais aussi la république séparatiste du Somaliland et le Burundi envisagent de rejoindre le mouvement. • L'est de la Centrafrique a été frappé ces derniers mois par plusieurs attaques attribuées à l’Armée de résistance du Seigneur (LRA), milice ougandaise tristement célèbre pour ses massacres et enlèvements d'enfants de masse dans les années 1990 et 2000. Recherché par la Cour pénale internationale depuis plus de 20 ans, son chef, Joseph Kony , demeure introuvable. Comment expliquer la résurgence de ce groupe ?

stories.title: États-Unis – Cameroun : Trump choisit l’artisan de ses accords d’expulsion comme ambassadeur à Yaoundé
stories.summary: Christian Jové Ehrhardt, responsable des très controversées expulsions de migrants vers des pays tiers, représente désormais Washington à Yaoundé. Une nomination qui éclaire les dessous de l’accord secret signé en décembre 2025 entre les États-Unis et le Cameroun.

stories.title: RDC: des opérations de l'AFC/M23 contre les FDLR visent systématiquement les civils, selon un rapport de l'ONU
stories.summary: RDC: des opérations de l'AFC/M23 contre les FDLR visent systématiquement les civils, selon un rapport de l'ONU Alors que Kinshasa défend un processus de désarmement des FDLR, ce groupe armé rwandais reste impliqué dans les violences au Nord-Kivu, un rapport du secrétaire général de l’ONU consulté par RFI décrit notamment des opérations de l’AFC/M23 contre ses combattants. Mais que se passe-t-il au-delà des affrontements ? Le document montre comment cette confrontation touche aussi les habitants. Publié le : 02/10/2026 - 06:36 1 min Temps de lecture Un combattant du M23 observe un groupe de FDLR à Goma, le 10 mai 2025. © AFP/Jospin Mwisha Par : RFI Publicité Lire la suite D'abord à Masisi, dans le Nord-Kivu, l’AFC/ M23 mène des opérations contre des éléments des Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR) et du groupe Nyatura. Le secrétaire général des Nations unies Antonio Guterres évoque au moins 60 corps qui auraient été découverts le 17 juin après ces opérations.

stories.title: A Johannesburg, la découverte de onze corps révèle l’ampleur des violences à l’égard des femmes
stories.summary: Depuis juillet, des corps de femmes nues ou à moitié nues, violemment battues, ont été retrouvés en banlieue de Johannesburg. Si la thèse du prédateur en série s’amenuise, la réalité d’une extrême violence infligée aux Sud-Africaines au quotidien s’impose.

stories.title: Making politics 'fun, trendy, sexy': How Gen Z could shape Kenya's next election
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters By Barbara Plett Usher Africa correspondent ,Â Reporting from Nairobi, Kangema & Meru Published 2 October 2026 Ademba Allans is making it "cool" to vote in Kenya. The student journalist turned civic mobiliser launched a voter registration drive on social media earlier this year, using snappy selfies infused with music and humour to target young people. The result astonished him and many observers of Kenyan politics â by the time the registration period ended, 2.6 million new voters across the country had signed up. He is aiming to get another 2.3 million on board in the next round. "It was the Gen Z way of doing politics," he tells me. "Fun, trendy, sexy, fashionable. Because of how we created the hype around it, people had the fear of missing out.

stories.title: A Flashy Zimbabwean Tycoon Who Befriended Presidents Dies in Crash
stories.summary: Wicknell Chivayo was riding in a helicopter with his wife when it plunged into a field. Dogged by corruption allegations, the businessman drew polarizing reactions even in death.

stories.title: Alan Ferguson obituary
stories.summary: Alan Ferguson, a fluent speaker of Swahili, worked for aid agencies in Kenya on family planning and public health View image in fullscreen Alan Ferguson, a fluent speaker of Swahili, worked for aid agencies in Kenya on family planning and public health Obituary Alan Ferguson obituary My brother, Alan Ferguson, who has died aged 79, was a Scotsman who began his working life as a geography lecturer at Nairobi University in Kenya , before working with aid agencies in that country. Alan joined the university in 1972, but left after a couple of years to teach in Britain at Cambridge University, and then in the US at NorthEastern University in Chicago. However, Kenya had got a hold on him, and he returned to work there, first for Amref , a Dutch organisation, and then GTZ, a German body, mainly in family planning and public health. Eventually he went freelance, helping various aid agencies with their work in Kenya, until a serious accident incapacitated him, forcing him to retire to Scotland. Born in Glasgow , Alan was the son of Bill, an analytical chemist, and Jessie (nee Moncrieff), a shorthand typist.

stories.title: Paiement instantané : Wave rallie la plateforme de la BCEAO et acte une nouvelle ère pour l’union monétaire
stories.summary: Avec sa plateforme de paiement instantanée, l’UEMOA entre dans l’ère du paiement interopérable entre banques et portefeuilles mobiles. Un bouleversement qui menace les revenus des opérateurs et redistribue les cartes.

stories.title: Pourquoi l’Algérie a élargi la peine de mort aux incendiaires et aux kidnappeurs d’enfants
stories.summary: Après les feux de forêts intenses et meurtriers de l’été, le chef de l’Etat, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a souhaité élargir le nombre de « crimes capitaux », passibles de la peine de mort. Le pays respectait pourtant un moratoire sur cette question depuis 1993.

stories.title: Cameroun : pourquoi Vision 4, la chaîne de télévision d’Amougou Belinga, a été suspendue
stories.summary: Incarcéré depuis deux ans dans le cadre de l’affaire Martinez Zogo, du nom du journaliste tué à Yaoundé en 2023, Jean-Pierre Amougou Belinga voit sa chaîne de télévision privée d’antenne pour un mois par le Conseil national de la communication. Un nouveau bras de fer s’engage donc avec le régulateur.

stories.title: Nigerian Charged With Running Fake Government Agency
stories.summary: The Nigerian secured office space in a federal building, opened bank accounts and even held meetings with foreign diplomats. He says he is innocent.

stories.title: L'AfCRA, une agence de notation africaine pour contrer les biais des géants mondiaux
stories.summary: Publicité L'AfCRA, une agence de notation africaine pour contrer les biais des géants mondiaux Analyse Afrique Le continent africain s'apprête à inaugurer sa propre agence de notation de crédit. Développée en collaboration avec l'Union Africaine, l'AfCRA compte fournir une évaluation du risque de crédit adaptée aux réalités africaines, face à des agences internationales régulièrement accusées de sévérité excessive envers l'Afrique. Publié le : 01/10/2026 - 19:50 4 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : David Rich L'Agence africaine de notation de crédit (AfCRA) ambitionne d'offrir une évaluation du risque de crédit plus équitable que les grandes agences de notation. © studio graphique FMM Moody's, Fitch, S&P... et maintenant l'AfCRA. L'Agence africaine de notation de crédit, spécifique au continent, sera inaugurée le 7 octobre à Port-Louis, capitale de l'Ile Maurice, où se trouve son siège. Développée par l' Union africaine mais conçue comme une institution indépendante, l'AfCRA a pour but d'offrir une évaluation du risque de crédit mieux adaptée aux réalités africaines et de faciliter l'accès à l'emprunt sur les marchés internationaux, qui demeure très difficile et cher pour un grand nombre de pays du continent.

stories.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties as northern conflict escalates
stories.summary: Image source, Reuters Image caption, More than 50 people have been killed since heavy fighting resumed in northern Ethiopia last week By Wycliffe Muia Published 2 October 2026 Ethiopia and Eritrea have severed diplomatic relations as renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia raises fears of a wider regional conflict. On Thursday, Ethiopia announced it was closing its embassy in the Eritrean capital, Asmara, and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave the country within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security. Eritrea responded by cutting diplomatic relations, saying Ethiopia's decision had left it with no choice but to take reciprocal action. Meanwhile, a pro-government militia says it has seized the town of Milazat, which is just 20km (12 miles) south-east of Mekelle, the capital of Tigray, where the main anti-government group is based. The BBC has not been able to verify this claim.

stories.title: Algeria introduces death penalty for arsonists after deadly wildfires
stories.summary: Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images By Doug Faulkner Published 1 October 2026 Algeria has adopted a law imposing the death penalty on people convicted of arson of forests or fields after a series of deadly wildfires swept parts of the country. Members of the national assembly voted through the bill, which also made child abduction a capital offence, on Thursday. Capital punishment has been in the country's penal code for some offences, but no execution has been carried out since 1993. The official death toll from the blazes stands at 12, but independent news outlets believe the figure to be much higher. Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the justice ministry to introduce the changes to the criminal law after more than 100 fires in the north-east of the country during an intense heatwave in northern Africa.

stories.title: Nigeria : comment des hommes politiques corrompus ont acheté "un bout d'Amérique"
stories.summary: Publicité Nigeria : comment des hommes politiques corrompus ont acheté "un bout d'Amérique" Afrique Un rapport publié par la plateforme de protection des lanceurs d'alerte en Afrique révèle avoir identifié près de 300 biens immobiliers aux États-Unis liés à des personnalités politiques nigérianes. Des propriétés acquises pour la plupart en liquide avec de l'argent public, alors que ces personnalités occupaient des fonctions officielles. Publié le : 01/10/2026 - 17:43 Modifié le : 01/10/2026 - 21:15 3 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Une vue de Los Angeles, en septembre 2026. La Californie fait partie des États où des biens immobiliers achetés par des personnalités politiques nigérianes ont été identifiés. © Michelle Mosqueda, Getty Images/AFP C'est un rapport qui lève une partie du voile sur l'ampleur de la corruption au Nigeria . La Plateforme de protection des lanceurs d'alerte en Afrique (PPLAAF) et l'Anti-Corruption Data Collective (ACDC) affirment dans ce document avoir identifié 284 propriétés immobilières aux États-Unis liées à 61 personnalités nigérianes qui occupent ou ont occupé des postes à responsabilité au sein de l'appareil d'État ou sécuritaire.

stories.title: Au Kenya, le lancement en un temps record du chantier de la raffinerie Dangote
stories.summary: Le magnat nigérian Aliko Dangote ambitionne de répliquer sa raffinerie de Lagos à Lamu, une région isolée face à l’océan Indien. Mercredi 30 septembre, en présence de chefs d’Etat africains, s’est tenue une cérémonie hautement politique et symbolique.

stories.title: En Egypte, l’arrestation de six journalistes d’un média d’investigation, signe de la nervosité du régime du président Al-Sissi
stories.summary: Ce coup de force sans précédent arrive au moment où les autorités doivent faire face à un contexte économique tendu et à des rivalités politiques qui s’aiguisent pour succéder au président Abdel Fattah Al-Sissi, au pouvoir depuis 2013.

stories.title: Zimbabwe tycoon Wicknell Chivayo and wife killed in helicopter crash
stories.summary: Image source, Wicknell Chivayo/Instagram Image caption, Wicknell Chivayo was a prominent businessman known for his extravagant lifestyle By Wycliffe Muia Published 1 October 2026 Prominent Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo and his wife have been killed in a helicopter crash that left six people dead, his family have confirmed. The helicopter came down in the Marondera rural area, about 70km (43 miles) east of the capital, Harare, on Wednesday evening. Police said all six people on board died. Family spokesperson Herbert Chivayo confirmed the deaths of the 43-year-old businessman and his wife Lucy Muteke to state broadcaster ZBC, saying the family was devastated by the tragedy. Chivayo was known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to some African presidents and lucrative government contracts that had repeatedly attracted scrutiny.

stories.title: 10 choses à savoir sur Justin Koné Katinan, bras droit de Laurent Gbagbo derrière les barreaux
stories.summary: Quatrième vice-président du PPA-CI, l’ancien ministre a été placé sous mandat de dépôt pour « actes de terrorisme ». Portrait d’un fidèle de longue date de Gbagbo, contraint à l’exil pendant plus d’une décennie, qui n’en est pas à sa première interpellation.

stories.title: Pourquoi l’Ethiopie replonge-t-elle dans la guerre ? Comprendre en trois minutes
stories.summary: Après plusieurs mois de tensions, les combats ont repris à la fin de septembre en Ethiopie entre l’armée fédérale éthiopienne et différents groupes rebelles, laissant planer la menace d’un nouveau conflit de grande ampleur. Une guerre civile avait déjà éclaté dans le pays entre 2020 et 2022.

stories.title: RDC : Walter Mbonyimwami fait le pari de l’IA pour explorer les mines du continent
stories.summary: RDC : Walter Mbonyimwami fait le pari de l’IA pour explorer les mines du continent Alors que la RDC abrite 70 % des réserves mondiales de cobalt et est le premier producteur de cuivre en Afrique, la start-up Synchros s’est fixé pour objectif de rationaliser l’exploitation minière grâce à la technologie numérique. Walter Mbonymwami, fondateur de la start-up Synchros. © Facebook Walter Mbonymwami Par Fatoumata Diallo Publié le 1 octobre à 11h53 Lecture : 5 minutes. Fichier généré le Lire dans l’app Issu du dossier Cap sur 2030 : qui façonne l’Afrique de demain ? Le continent n’a jamais compté autant d’entreprises valant plus de 1 milliard de dollars. Mais, pour s’affirmer comme des leaders, elles doivent encore trouver la parade aux difficultés propres à cinq enjeux clés : énergie, financement, transformation, nouvelles technologies et fragmentation des marchés.

stories.title: Au Maroc, malgré la nomination d’une première ministre, le plafond de verre demeure pour les femmes
stories.summary: Sur 395 députés élus au Parlement après le scrutin du 23 septembre, la représentation des femmes reste minoritaire (107) et cantonnée aux quotas. Toutefois, la nomination de Fatima Ezzahra El-Mansouri par le roi suscite l’espoir des associations féministes.

stories.title: Pétrole : pourquoi Abidjan invite Murphy Oil à intensifier ses forages
stories.summary: Après avoir fait de l’offshore ivoirien sa porte d’entrée sur le continent en attendant d’étendre ses opérations au Maroc et au Cameroun via de nouveaux permis, Murphy Oil fait déjà face à un premier test décisif proposé par Abidjan.

stories.title: Interdiction des importations françaises: un pas de plus dans la crise franco-algérienne
stories.summary: Applicable depuis juillet 2026 mais sans avoir fait l’objet d’une communication officielle auprès des entreprises concernées, l’interdiction d’importer des marchandises françaises met de nombreux partenaires algériens en difficulté. Et vient encore dégrader une relation déjà glaciale.

stories.title: Au Ghana, le retour au calme à Bawku signe-t-il vraiment le recul de la violence jihadiste venue du Burkina Faso ?
stories.summary: Bawku connaît un calme inédit : plus de 130 jours sans violence, dans une ville meurtrie par des décennies de conflits ethniques. Médiation, pression sécuritaire et lassitude des communautés expliquent ce fragile répit.

stories.title: Dangote: 'Nobody can make Africa great but us'
stories.summary: Dangote: 'Nobody can make Africa great but us' Dangote: 'Nobody can make Africa great but us' Close "Nobody can make Africa great but us," were the words of Africa's richest man Aliko Dangote as he urged Africans to take the fate of their continent in their own hands, rather than relying on foreigners. In an exclusive interview with BBC Focus on Africa's Nkechi Ogbonna, Dangote answered quick-fire questions on a wide array of topics - from the main problem of the continent to the opportunities for its youth and Africa's main strengths. stories.title: ‘They raped our country’: documentary follows Kenyans’ fight for restitution over stolen land
stories.summary: Much of the land taken during the colonial era has remained with the political elite and foreign companies occupying huge tea plantations. Photograph: Andrew H Brown View image in fullscreen Much of the land taken during the colonial era has remained with the political elite and foreign companies occupying huge tea plantations. Photograph: Andrew H Brown ‘They raped our country’: documentary follows Kenyans’ fight for restitution over stolen land Multinational tea companies still occupy ancestral highlands of communities displaced during British colonial era F or British colonialists, the fertile and cool uplands of central Kenya were the “White Highlands”, to be reserved exclusively for European settlers. Local communities were forced from the land, which was turned into plantations for tea and other crops. In recent decades, descendants of the displaced have fought to reclaim their ancestral land, some of which is now occupied by multinational tea companies and other large corporations.

stories.title: Morocco’s King Names a Female Prime Minister, in a Historic First
stories.summary: Morocco became the second North African country to have a woman lead the government with the selection of Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a lawyer and politician from the centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party.

stories.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
stories.summary: Afrikaner refugees from South Africa hold American flags as they arrive at Dulles airport in Washington last May. Photograph: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP View image in fullscreen Afrikaner refugees from South Africa hold American flags as they arrive at Dulles airport in Washington last May. Photograph: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad Support such as for white Afrikaners and anti-communism reveals how US is redefining what qualifies as human rights With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”. On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests not to do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The state department declined to comment on questions from the Guardian specifically on whether it had obligated the funds and had “blown” holds from Congress due to concerns about the money’s use.

stories.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5NX1O Prospective migrants who arrived in Greece are taken into a migration hub Image: Sofia Kleftaki/DW Advertisement Deportation centers are legally contentious, expensive and the subject of political controversy: For years, Brussels has been grappling with the issue of establishing such centers outside the EU for rejected asylum seekers. Previous attempts have failed due to legal objections, but now, a "group of five" consisting of Greece , Germany , Austria , Denmark and the Netherlands believes it has overcome these hurdles . During an interview with the Greek television channel ANT1, Greece's Minister of Migration, Thanos Plevris, stated that the first of these so-called " return hubs " is scheduled to begin operations as early as the second half of 2027 — just in time for Greece to assume the EU Council Presidency. Plevris said Greece had chosen an African country but could not reveal its name yet. Diplomatic circles and media outlets close to the EU have repeatedly cited Rwanda or Uganda , but neither country has been confirmed as the location.

stories.title: Dans le nord du Nigeria, le nombre d’enlèvements augmente sous la pression de gangs criminels locaux et des djihadistes
stories.summary: Au moins 87 personnes ont été kidnappées samedi et dimanche dans les Etats de Zamfara et du Niger. Entre juillet 2025 et juin 2026, on dénombrait 7 825 victimes de prises d’otage, un chiffre en hausse qui fragilise le pouvoir, avant l’élection présidentielle de janvier 2027.

stories.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5NRVf Senegal have refurbished some of their existing facilities rather than just building new ones Image: Cem Özdel/Anadolu/IMAGO Advertisement At the end of October 2026, the first ever Olympic event on African soil will take place as the Youth Olympics comes to Senegal . Around 2,700 young athletes are expected to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports, with many qualifying through the African Youth Games last year. "We were entrusted with hosting this event and that is why from Johannesburg to Nairobi, from Dakar to Djbouti, it is all of young Africa that is watching you and watching you with pride," Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye said at the arrival of the flame. The moment marks yet another step forward for global sport in Africa. In 2025, the first major road cycling event took place on the continent, and in September this year it was announced the first-ever World Athletics Championships would be held in Kenya in 2029. There are also on-going negotiations about Formula 1 returning.

stories.title: Kenya: la méga-raffinerie Dangote «va permettre à une grande partie de l'Afrique de l'Est» de devenir autosuffisante
stories.summary: Le grand invité Afrique Kenya: la méga-raffinerie Dangote «va permettre à une grande partie de l'Afrique de l'Est» de devenir autosuffisante Publié le : 02/10/2026 - 06:55 C'est à Lamu, au Kenya, que le milliardaire nigérian Aliko Dangote a posé mercredi 30 septembre la première pierre de sa nouvelle méga-raffinerie, qui devrait ouvrir d'ici à 2030. Plusieurs chefs d'État africains ont assisté au lancement du projet qui vise à rendre l'Afrique autosuffisante pour sa consommation de produits pétroliers. Mais pourquoi l'homme le plus riche d'Afrique a-t-il décidé de construire une méga-raffinerie au Kenya, où il n'y a pratiquement pas de pétrole ? Benjamin Augé, chercheur associé à l'Institut français des relations internationales, répond aux questions de Christophe Boisbouvier. De gauche à droite : le Premier ministre éthiopien Abiy Ahmed, le président ougandais Yoweri Museveni, le président kenyan William Ruto, le PDG du groupe Dangote Aliko Dangote, l'ancien président nigérian Olusegun Obasanjo et le président béninois Romuald Wadagni assistent à la cérémonie de pose de la première pierre d'une raffinerie de pétrole d'Afrique de l'Est à Lamu, au Kenya, le 30 septembre 2026. © Monicah Mwangi / Reuters Publicité RFI : Quand Aliko Dangote dit que cette méga raffinerie va permettre à l'Afrique de devenir autosuffisante en carburant, est-ce que c'est vrai ?

stories.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
stories.summary: South Africa has been gripped with grief and fury after the discovery of 11 women’s bodies dumped across Ekurhuleni, a city adjoining Johannesburg, since 15 July. Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters View image in fullscreen South Africa has been gripped with grief and fury after the discovery of 11 women’s bodies dumped across Ekurhuleni, a city adjoining Johannesburg, since 15 July. Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unsolved murders, attempted murders and serious sexual offences against women and children, as well as producing a funded plan to reduce the forensic backlog for such cases, both within 60 days.

stories.title: Cotton Queen review – mystery, matriarchs and magic in pioneering Sudanese debut
stories.summary: Can she shape her own future? … Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud as Al-Sit and Mihad Murtada as Nafisa in Cotton Queen. Photograph: Frida Marzouk View image in fullscreen Can she shape her own future? … Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud as Al-Sit and Mihad Murtada as Nafisa in Cotton Queen. Photograph: Frida Marzouk Review Cotton Queen review – mystery, matriarchs and magic in pioneering Sudanese debut Suzannah Mirghani’s first feature contains a powerful performance by Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud as a village’s elder woman and tackles the long shadow of British imperialism and women’s rights ‘I decide my past,” says a village matriarch in this intriguingly political and poetic drama from Suzannah Mirghani, making her feature debut – and with it becoming the first Sudanese woman to direct a feature. (She was forced to cancel the original shoot in Sudan when war broke out in 2023 , moving production to Egypt.) It’s a film with things to say about the long shadow of the British empire, neocolonialism, women’s rights and female genital mutilation. But it mostly says it all without undermining its sense of mystery and shivers of magic realism. We’re in present day Sudan , where village elder Al-Sit (Rabha Mohamed Mahmoud) is an iron-willed woman not to be messed with.

stories.title: The journalist crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute
stories.summary: Image source, Ngabo Amon/BBC By Basillioh Rukanga Â and Â Bella Twine ,Â BBC Focus on Africa Published 29 September 2026 Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma has been crowned king of Uganda's Tooro kingdom. The new monarch has long been a familiar face in the East African nation, where for many he was known not as the heir to the throne, but as a storyteller: a long-serving anchor and editor at the state broadcaster. But the 56-year-old - now King Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma Nyabongo I - has become the subject of media attention himself as his rise to the Tooro throne sparked controversy and widespread reactions beyond the country. Tooro is one of Uganda's four main officially recognised historical kingdoms. For the last 31 years, it had been headed by King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who was once known as a "boy king", after ascending to the throne as an infant.

A dearth of opportunity at home incentivises young men in particular to take huge risks to reach the European Union.

stories.title: Son of Zambian bishop detained in post-election raid fears for his father's safety
stories.summary: Son of Zambian bishop detained in post-election raid fears for his father's safety Son of Zambian bishop detained in post-election raid fears for his father's safety Close The son of detained Zambian opposition politician Bishop Trevor Mwamba has told the BBC he is concerned for his father's safety after the former Bishop of Botswana was detained along with 10 other opposition figures by authorities. Eno Mwamba said his father, who is leader of the United National Independence Party, has been charged with treason following President Hakainde Hichilema's disputed election victory. The opposition politicians have been held since a raid by security forces on 14 August. Opposition leader Brian Mundubile, head of the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP), had gone into hiding after disputing the election result, but has since also been detained by the authorities. The government accuses the opposition of planning an armed insurgency and have charged the detained politicians with treason.

stories.summary: Jean Claude Njara standing alongside his sister, Rasoa, with a portrait of his son. Photograph: Aina Zo Raberanto/The Guardian Murdered for their eyes: people with albinism living in terror in Madagascar The country is struggling to address a rise in attacks, with a record 13 people – mostly children – killed this year for body parts, which some believe can bring good fortune Not long after midnight in late May this year, three men barged through the door of the small room where Nicole Soalala lived with her family on the outskirts of Toliara, a coastal city in the south of Madagascar . Her husband got up to ask what they wanted, but they attacked him with a piece of wood and an axe. Soalala, 32, grabbed her youngest child, Landricia – an 18-month-old girl with albinism – and hoisted her on to her back, holding her there with a piece of fabric she started to wrap around herself.

stories.title: Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July. Here's what we know so far
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, The discovery of 12 bodies in an area east of Johannesburg has sparked alarm in South Africa By Khanyisile Ngcobo Reporting from Johannesburg Published 28 September 2026 Police in South Africa have confirmed the discovery of the bodies of three more women in an area east of Johannesburg, bringing the total number of bodies found there to 12 in just two months. The latest bodies were found in Ekurhuleni between Saturday and Monday morning, according to local police. Police have made arrests in three of the cases, which do not appear to be related to the others. Nevertheless, police have said they cannot rule out the possibility of a serial killer. The discoveries have caused widespread alarm in Ekurhuleni, particularly around Kempton Park, and come against the backdrop of longstanding concerns about high levels of violence against women in South Africa.

Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported. stories.title: Banished: the secret Trump deals sending migrants across the world - podcast
stories.summary: 00:00:00 00:00:00 Banished: the secret Trump deals sending migrants across the world - podcast Investigations correspondent Louisa Loveluck reports on the Trump administration’s secret deportation deals, sending thousands of migrants to ‘third countries’ across the world A Sierra Leonean nurse detained, handcuffed and flown to Ghana. An Iranian dissident to Central African Republic . A Cameroonian to Equatorial Guinea. This is the face of the Trump administration’s deportations policy since 2025 – striking deals with 35 countries, and sending up to 25,000 migrants in the US across the world, often to places they have no connection to at all. The Guardian investigations correspondent Louisa Loveluck – as part of a consortium of journalists organised by Forbidden Stories – uncovers some of the human stories behind these deals.

Photograph: Esa Alexander/Reuters At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say Seventeen people killed near Johannesburg in suspected ‘illegal goldmining turf war’, as 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police. The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.

Photograph: Nic Bothma/Reuters ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents . The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.
